runtime_unusable.label: Runtime cannot use it
runtime_unusable.summary: The card is listed and looks well, but the accelerator runtime could not use it: creating a context on it failed.
runtime_unusable.action: Check the driver errors in the node's dmesg. One card that fails to initialize can make every card of a host unusable, so look at the other cards' findings too; the usual fix is a reset of the failing card, sometimes a host reboot.

telemetry_unavailable.label: Diagnostic data unavailable
telemetry_unavailable.summary: The card can be identified, but a diagnostic field such as the ECC counter was not reported as a valid number.
telemetry_unavailable.action: Inspect the recorded field and driver configuration. Scheduling remains enabled; missing telemetry is not a claim of zero errors.

inventory_identity_invalid.label: Invalid card identity
inventory_identity_invalid.summary: The vendor inventory returned missing, duplicate, or inconsistent card identity fields.
inventory_identity_invalid.action: Inspect the card_validation evidence and compare xpu-smi output with PCI and device mappings.

vendor_cli_unanswered.label: Not readable
vendor_cli_unanswered.summary: The card is bound to its vendor driver, but the vendor tool did not answer this round, so nothing is known about the card beyond its PCI identity. The driver may well be fine.
vendor_cli_unanswered.action: Look at the node's GPU probe error for why the tool did not answer, and run the vendor smi command by hand on the node. A tool that hangs usually means the driver is stuck on one card.

driver_init_failed.label: Driver init failed
driver_init_failed.summary: The card is bound to its vendor driver, but the driver could not bring it up, so nothing can use it and the vendor tool does not list it.
driver_init_failed.action: Check the driver errors in the node's dmesg (for NVIDIA: NVRM lines such as "RmInitAdapter failed"). The card usually needs a reset, and sometimes the host needs a reboot; where the card is not meant for this host, unbind it from the vendor driver.

pcie_link_degraded.label: PCIe link degraded
pcie_link_degraded.summary: A PCIe link between the card and its root port runs at fewer lanes (or, while the card is busy, a lower speed) than both of its ends support, report after report. The card still works but loads models and moves data more slowly, so it is used only when healthy cards run out.
pcie_link_degraded.action: Use the command below to see what both ends of the link support and what they negotiated. It is usually a badly seated card, a riser or cable, or a slot set to a lower speed in the BIOS; check and reseat it while the host is idle.

pcie_errors.label: PCIe errors
pcie_errors.summary: PCIe devices between the card and its root port reported new recovered errors. The card still works and recovers on its own after 15 minutes without new errors.
pcie_errors.action: Use the command below to see the error counters, and look for AER entries in dmesg. Errors that keep coming usually mean a signal problem in the link or slot.

pcie_fatal_errors.label: PCIe fatal errors
pcie_fatal_errors.summary: PCIe devices between the card and its root port reported new fatal errors, after which the link has to be reset. The card is not given work until a runtime check passes on it again.
pcie_fatal_errors.action: Use the command below to see the error counters, and look for AER entries in dmesg. The card usually needs a reset or the host a reboot; if it keeps happening, contact the hardware vendor.

nvlink_down.label: NVLink down
nvlink_down.summary: Fewer of this card's NVLinks are active than it has had, two checks in a row. The card still works, but work spread across cards is slower, and the scheduler no longer groups it with the cards it was linked to.
nvlink_down.action: Use the command below to see each link's state and error counters, and look for Xid 74 in dmesg. It usually needs a card reset or a host reboot; on NVSwitch systems also check the Fabric Manager.

memory_repair_pending.label: Reset pending
memory_repair_pending.summary: Memory rows or pages on this card are marked for replacement; the replacement takes effect at the next reset.
memory_repair_pending.action: Reset the card with the command below when it is idle; if the reset does not succeed, reboot the host.

memory_uncorrectable_errors.label: Memory fault
memory_uncorrectable_errors.summary: The card has had uncorrectable memory errors since the driver loaded or the card was last reset.
memory_uncorrectable_errors.action: Reset the card with the command below when it is idle; if the error count grows again after the reset, contact the hardware vendor.

memory_remap_failed.label: Memory fault
memory_remap_failed.summary: A memory row on this card could not be replaced.

reset_required.label: Reset required
reset_required.summary: The driver reported an event that requires a card reset to recover.
reset_required.action: Reset the card with the command below when it is idle.

reboot_required.label: Host reboot required
reboot_required.summary: The driver reported an event that requires a host reboot to recover.
reboot_required.action: Reboot the host when it is idle.

power_cycle_required.label: Power cycle required
power_cycle_required.summary: The driver reported an event that requires powering the host off and on again to recover.
power_cycle_required.action: Power the host off and on again.

vendor_health_warning.label: Warning
vendor_health_warning.summary: The vendor tool reports this card at Warning; the error code and information state the cause.
vendor_health_warning.action: Look up the error code in the vendor documentation.

vendor_health_fault.label: Fault
vendor_health_fault.summary: The vendor tool reports this card at Alarm or Critical; the error code and information state the cause.
vendor_health_fault.action: Look up the error code in the vendor documentation.

memory_error_history.label: OK
memory_error_history.summary: The card has a history of memory errors whose pages were retired or rows replaced. The counter is cumulative and a reset does not clear it.

inventory_incomplete.summary: The driver card count differs from its inventory rows. Verified cards remain available; the inventory may be incomplete.
inventory_incomplete.action: Compare the vendor inventory with PCI devices and check the driver log. Missing card identities are not guessed.
inventory_incomplete.label: Incomplete inventory

healthCheck.title: Health check
healthCheck.help: When on, the server sends the service one minimal request through the gateway every minute: a chat model gets the message "1" and generates 1 token, an embedding model embeds "1". A reply within the threshold is healthy, none by then a timeout, an error or an unreachable replica a failure; nothing is sent while no replica is running awake. The check only reports: it never restarts or removes a replica, and it is not counted in the request figures. Changing it needs no restart.
healthCheck.recentMean: {{ok}} of the last {{count}} answered in time, {{time}} on average
healthCheck.recentNone: None of the last {{count}} answered in time
healthCheck.noReplicaHelp: No replica is running awake, so no check was sent
healthCheck.unsupported: This model serves neither chat nor embeddings, so it cannot be checked

tokenize.title: Tokenize API
tokenize.help: When on, the gateway forwards POST /v1/tokenize and /v1/detokenize to the engine, chosen by the request's model like any other /v1 request. They only run the tokenizer: they are not counted in the request figures and leave no request record. Changing it needs no restart.
tokenize.otherEngine: vLLM and SGLang serve tokenize; another engine may not, and then the request gets the engine's own error
